Here is a paragraph using words that contain only three types of vowels:

"Ape ate a pet. The cat sat on a mat. The rat ran to the cat's mat. The ape ate the rat. The cat sat on the mat. The rat ran to the ape's mat."

And here is the timeline of mankind:

The first caveman, Gronk, emerged from the primordial ooze, blinking in the bright light of a new world. He stumbled and fell, but rose again, driven by the primal urge to survive. As the ages passed, Gronk's tribe grew, and with it, the complexity of human society. The pyramids rose, the empires fell, and the ages passed in a blur of blood and fire.

But then, without warning, the universe itself began to unravel. A strange, pulsating energy enveloped the Earth, and Gronk felt himself being pulled apart and put back together again. When the energy dissipated, Gronk found himself standing on a vast, green plain, surrounded by an endless sea of identical replicas of himself. The other Gronks were just as confused, just as frightened, as he was.

As the ages passed, the replicas of Gronk began to evolve and adapt, forming new tribes and civilizations. Some built great cities, while others retreated to the wilderness, living in harmony with the natural world. The replicas of Gronk also began to explore the infinite Earth, discovering new lands and meeting new versions of themselves.

Centuries passed, and the replicas of Gronk continued to evolve and adapt. They built great machines, harnessed the power of the stars, and explored the depths of space. They created art, music, and literature, leaving behind a legacy of beauty and wisdom.

And yet, despite all their advancements, the replicas of Gronk remained fundamentally the same. They were still driven by the same primal urges, still bound by the same desires and fears. They were still human.

As the ages passed, the replicas of Gronk began to fade, one by one, until only one remained. The last astronaut, a lone figure in a suit of gleaming white, stood on the edge of a vast, empty plain. The infinite Earth stretched out before him, a sea of identical replicas of himself, each one a reminder of the infinite possibilities that had been lost.

The astronaut took a deep breath, and stepped forward, into the unknown. The infinite Earth stretched out before him, a vast, uncharted territory, waiting to be explored. And in that moment, the astronaut knew that he was not alone. He was part of a vast, interconnected web of humanity, a web that stretched across the infinite expanse of the Earth.

The astronaut smiled, and took another step forward, into the unknown. The infinite Earth stretched out before him, a sea of possibilities, waiting to be explored. And in that moment, the astronaut knew that he was home.
